title: Tamarind and Honey-Glazed Roast Turkey
author: Pierre Thiam (SAVEUR)
desc: A 12-lb turkey roasted 1 hour at 450°, 1 hour at 350° under foil, then 30 minutes more basted every 10 minutes with a tamarind, honey and fish-sauce glaze until the thigh reads 160°; the pan juices thickened into a gravy.
longDesc: Pierre Thiam’s Thanksgiving turkey, published by SAVEUR on 16 November 2015 (serves 6–8; total time 3 hours 45 minutes). The glaze: 6 oz of coarsely chopped tamarind pulp is covered with 1/2 cup of boiling water and left 10 minutes, broken up with the fingers, left 5 minutes more, pressed through a fine sieve and the solids discarded; honey, fish sauce, garlic and chile are stirred in until smooth; you should have 1 1/2 cups. The turkey is set on a rack, seasoned inside and out, stock poured in the pan, and roasted at 450° about 1 hour until golden brown; the oven is lowered to 350°, the bird covered with foil and roasted about 1 more hour until almost cooked through; the foil comes off and it roasts about 30 more minutes, basted with the glaze every 10 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thigh reads 160°. It rests 20 minutes under foil. The pan juices are boiled with the cornstarch slurry about 5 minutes until thickened and strained. THE PAGE PRINTS THE BASTING QUANTITY AS ‘12 cup’ — a suspected lost fraction slash (1/2 cup?) that is NOT determinable from the page and is left as printed. Use fresh ‘wet’ tamarind pulp; the page says concentrate or syrup is too sweet.
ingredients: 6 oz tamarind pulp, coarsely chopped (fresh ‘wet’ pulp sold in blocks with seeds mixed in)
1/4 cup Vietnamese or Thai fish sauce
1 Scotch bonnet or habanero chile, stemmed, seeded and finely chopped
One 12-lb turkey, rinsed and dried thoroughly
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper — quantities not printed
steps: Cover the tamarind with 1/2 cup boiling water and let soften 10 minutes. Break it apart with your fingers and let sit 5 more minutes. Press through a fine sieve over a bowl and discard the solids. Stir in the honey, fish sauce, garlic and chile until smooth. You should have 1 1/2 cups.
Heat the oven to 450°. Set the turkey on a rack in a large roasting pan and season the cavity and outside generously. Pour the stock into the pan and roast about 1 hour, until golden brown.
Lower the oven to 350°, cover with foil and roast about 1 more hour, until almost cooked through.

Remove the foil and roast about 30 more minutes, basting with the tamarind glaze every 10 minutes (the page prints the basting quantity as ‘12 cup’), until an instant-read thermometer in the thigh reads 160°.

Move the turkey on its rack to a cutting board, tent with foil and rest 20 minutes. Pour the pan juices into a small saucepan. Stir the cornstarch into the 2 tablespoons of cold water and stir the slurry into the juices. Boil over medium-high heat, stirring, about 5 minutes, until thickened. Strain through a fine sieve and serve with the turkey.
chefTips: Printed cues: ‘golden brown’, ‘almost cooked through’, thigh at 160°, gravy ‘thickened’.
The glaze makes 1 1/2 cups; the page says to baste with ‘12 cup’ — decide the quantity yourself, since it is not determinable from the page.
Use wet tamarind pulp, not concentrate.
commonMistakes: Using tamarind concentrate or syrup, which the page says is too sweet.
Basting before the foil comes off.
healthBenefits: A large roast; the glaze is honey-sweet.
culturalNote: Tamarind pulp is ‘a prized ingredient in Senegal’, made into candies, mixed into a cooling drink or spooned over grilled fish; the glaze ‘lend[s] an umami depth to this unexpected Thanksgiving roast turkey’. A Pierre Thiam holiday recipe, not a traditional Senegalese dish.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Tamarind and Honey-Glazed Roast Turkey’ (the parent article links it as ‘Tamarind-Glazed Roast Turkey’). Byline as printed: ‘By Pierre Thiam’. SAVEUR, 16 November 2015. Serves 6–8 (7 used); total time 3 hours 45 minutes. TWO-PASS on every quantity, including the suspected misprint.

SUSPECTED MISPRINT, TWO-PASS, reported as printed and NOT corrected: the basting quantity is printed ‘12 cup’. Step 1 prints a yield of 1 1/2 cups of glaze and a 1/2 cup of boiling water, so a lost fraction slash is likely, but the value is not determinable from the page.

Times: glaze 10 + 5 minutes (rest), turkey rest 20 minutes (rest 35); roast about 1 hour + about 1 hour + about 30 minutes plus about 5 minutes for the gravy (cook 155); the prep of 35 is a scheduling split of the printed 3 hours 45 minutes. ABSENT: salt and pepper amounts.
